title: SPARK CSEC Physics - Paper 01 Practice Paper 2
subject: Physics
syllabus: CXC 22/G/SYLL 13, for examinations from May and June 2015
instructions: This test consists of 60 items. You will have 1 hour and 15 minutes to answer them.
In addition to this test booklet, you should have an answer sheet.
Each item in this test has four suggested answers lettered (A), (B), (C), (D). Read each item you are about to answer and decide which choice is best.
On your answer sheet, find the number which corresponds to your item and shade the space having the same letter as the answer you have chosen.
If you want to change your answer, erase it completely before you fill in your new choice.
When you are told to begin, turn the page and work as quickly and as carefully as you can. If you cannot answer an item, go on to the next one. You may return to that item later.
You may do any rough work in this booklet.
Figures are not necessarily drawn to scale.
You may use a silent, non-programmable calculator to answer items.

stimulus.alt: A measuring cylinder graduated from 0 to 50 cm cubed in steps of 5, containing a liquid whose meniscus is level with the 32 mark.

items.stem: The volume of the liquid, in cm³, is

misconception.label: Read the nearest labelled graduation instead of counting the small divisions.
Read the top of the meniscus, where the liquid climbs the glass, instead of the bottom.
Miscounted the small divisions between 30 and 35.

steps: The graduations are labelled every 5 cm³ and there are five small divisions between them, so one small division is 1 cm³.
For a liquid that wets the glass the surface is concave, and the reading is taken at the bottom of the curve.
The bottom of the meniscus is two small divisions above 30, so the volume is 32 cm³.

items.objective_statement: draw a line of ‘best fit’ for a set of plotted values
items.stem: A line of best fit drawn through a set of plotted points should

options.text: pass through the first and last points

misconception.label: Those two points are no more reliable than the others.

options.text: pass through the origin in every case

misconception.label: It passes through the origin only if the physics requires it.

options.text: have roughly as many points above it as below it
join each point to the next

misconception.label: That is a dot to dot line, not a best fit line.

steps: The best fit line is the best available average of all the points, so they should be balanced on either side of it.
solution.answer_line: have roughly as many points above it as below it

items.objective_statement: identify situations in which the application of a force will result in a turning effect
items.stem: Pushing a door at the point closest to its hinge produces almost no turning effect because

options.text: friction in the hinge is too great

misconception.label: Friction is not the reason.
The same force further out would turn the door easily.

options.text: the perpendicular distance from the pivot is almost zero

misconception.label: The weight of the door is not the reason.

steps: The moment is force times perpendicular distance from the pivot, and that distance is nearly zero at the hinge.

items.objective_statement: calculate the change in gravitational potential energy using Ep = mgh
items.stem: A load of mass 5 kg is lifted through a vertical height of 2 m. Taking g as 10 N/kg, the gain in potential energy is

misconception.label: This multiplies by an extra factor of ten.
This omits g.
This uses ½mv² by mistake.

steps: The gain in potential energy is the work done against gravity, Ep = mgh. Substituting, Ep = 5 × 10 × 2 = 100 J. The mass is already in kilograms and the height is the vertical height, so no conversion is needed.

items.stem: When the strip is heated strongly it will

misconception.label: Both metals expand, but by different amounts, so the strip cannot stay straight.

options.text: bend so that the brass is on the outside of the curve
bend so that the iron is on the outside of the curve

misconception.label: The iron expands less, so it takes the inside of the curve.

items.stem: The distance labelled X is the
